verdict.root_cause: The ad service stopped existing on the network at 12:25:29 and did not return. Its own log shows clean traffic up to the final second, then an orderly JVM shutdown-hook teardown of the gRPC ads server and total silence afterwards [tr_fb2d7b15b665]; one second later the change log records platform-automation setting ad's image reference from unset to the 2.2.0-ad-hotfix.2 tag [tr_2ab1b562f262]. From 12:30 the frontend logs gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE against one peer, 172.18.0.19:9555 (the conventional ad port), with a host-unreachable connect error — no TCP session is ever established, so the peer is absent rather than refusing or hanging [tr_fe847d5db367]. The deploy action terminated the running replica and no healthy replacement came up on that address: the artifact that should be running is not running. The frontend and frontend-proxy alerts are caller-side propagation of the missing dependency.
verdict.reasoning: ad's log ends at an explicit graceful shutdown at 12:25:29 with no error ramp, no OOM and no panic, and the specialist confirmed the silence is a real service state rather than a retention artifact [tr_fb2d7b15b665]. An image-reference change lands one second later from the same automation actor that has been oscillating this service between one hotfix tag and unset [tr_2ab1b562f262] — a shutdown hook firing at that instant is the orchestrator replacing the replica. The caller's symptom matches a missing peer exactly: status 14 with a host-unreachable transport error to a single address, explicitly distinguished from connection-refused, from application-level errors, and from slow-but-connected saturation [tr_fe847d5db367]. This rules out process_freeze (a frozen process keeps accepting and hangs callers) and network_partition (a running-but-cut-off ad would log its own unreachability; ad logs nothing after a self-initiated stop). Both metric dispatches on ad were rejected with HTTP 400 and returned no data on restarts, availability or resources [tr_361e4ee9a7d6], which is the main gap.
open_questions: Did a replacement ad pod ever start — crashlooping, stuck pulling the hotfix tag, or never scheduled? No availability or restart metric was retrieved; both queries failed with HTTP 400 [tr_361e4ee9a7d6].
The frontend log names only 172.18.0.19:9555, not a service name; ad attribution rests on port convention plus the coincident shutdown [tr_fe847d5db367].

The same tag was applied and reverted repeatedly earlier in the week without this outcome [tr_2ab1b562f262], so the defect may lie in the automation leaving zero replicas rather than in the image itself.

alternatives.root_cause: The ad replica was evicted or descheduled under node resource pressure, and the graceful shutdown is the SIGTERM path of that eviction.
alternatives.why_not: An eviction and a rollout give the same orderly shutdown signature, but only the deploy is independently corroborated by a change record one second before the shutdown line [tr_2ab1b562f262], and ad's final minute shows no degradation ramp [tr_fb2d7b15b665]. No resource metric exists either way.

alternatives.root_cause: The host-unreachable errors reflect a network/routing fault isolating ad's address from the frontend rather than ad's absence.
alternatives.why_not: A partitioned ad would still be running and logging; instead ad recorded a completed, self-initiated shutdown and emitted nothing at all afterwards [tr_fb2d7b15b665].

proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if ad logs show startup then another shutdown or a stack trace (image genuinely bad / crashloop), or stay empty (never scheduled or pull failure — fix lies in platform-automation, outside this system, escalate), or if frontend keeps logging host-unreachable to 172.18.0.19:9555 after ad is up, meaning the port-convention attribution was wrong.
proposal.risk: If the real defect is the automation leaving zero replicas rather than the image, this restores service only until the next apply/revert cycle (~10-20 min) and masks the loop. The recreate itself discards ad's in-process cache and briefly resets any connection that had recovered.
